bluf: Madwire is a Fort Collins, CO technology company, founded 2009 and family run by founders JB Kellogg (CEO) and Joe Kellogg, selling business management and marketing software plus services to small businesses and franchises from one platform, Marketing 360. It claims 15,000 active clients, 500+ staff and 3,600+ reviews averaging 4.6+, and names none of the clients. The record holds no moves, news, jobs, AI posture or pricing, and the sitemap of 81 URLs had 0 updates in 365 days. The Monsoon read puts it at Landfall, 71.7, displacement 81.7: the SMB book buys on price and its web and local hours are the most movable in the record.
doing:
Madwire positions as a technology company selling business management and marketing software plus services to small businesses and franchises from a single platform: a software subscription with marketing services attached, sold to small firms rather than retained by named accounts. Its headline claim is 15,000 active clients and 3,600+ reviews averaging a 4.6+ rating; the record holds the numbers with no case study, client name or result behind them, at low confidence.

The sold mix has no lead line; three lines score 2 and read as core. Email & CRM rests on the meta description selling business management software and a platform that handles leads, customers, appointments and payments. Local rests on the Top Rated Local brand, which ranks nearby businesses by its Rating Score, with listings and reviews inside the platform. Web & Product rests on Websites 360, billed as the #1 website platform for small business, and a homepage websites block. Content and PR, creator, paid search and paid social score 1 with no evidence note; SEO, AI search, AI automation, data and measurement, CRO, B2B, programmatic and retail media score 0. The service list adds payments, appointments, online reviews, business listings, social media, content marketing and multi channel digital advertising. Proprietary lines are Marketing 360, Websites 360, Top Rated Local and Rating Score; the record lists no partners.

Its AI posture is absent: the record holds no AI line, no AI search capability (P1 absent) and no AI URLs in the sitemap, itself a finding for a platform selling to 15,000 small businesses. The record lists no dated moves, no news, no case studies, no jobs and no pricing signals. Conspicuously absent for a company of its kind: a published price, any SEO or paid search evidence beyond a score of 1, any client name, a CMS reading for its own site, and any own advertising in the Google or LinkedIn libraries.
clients:
The record reads the client type as SMB and lists one vertical, franchise; the home market is the US from Fort Collins, CO, the one office listed, with 500+ staff claimed. The needs read holds 0 clients: no case study, no logo, no press release and no slug names an account, so nothing is observed, nothing is named only and nothing is shared with another tracked agency. The headline claim of 15,000 active clients makes the silence the finding: the book is a subscriber count, not a set of named engagements, and a rival cannot contest a named account from this record because there is none. The prominence signal, the About page claiming 15,000 active clients and 500+ staff, is the only client evidence on file.

What the base needs next is inferred from the sold mix, since no client signal exists. Small businesses and franchises buying a website builder, listings, reviews and a CRM from one platform sit under KJ7 (local discovery is being enclosed), the judgment the Horus read marks Madwire exposed to through its local line, and KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), its most exposed. It is very likely, moderate confidence, that these subscribers will need LSA and Sponsored Places work that the P3 read says the platform does not yet show, and likely, low confidence, that the same subscribers will ask the platform for AI answer visibility it has no line for; the KJ8 tailwind (human provenance as a distribution signal) runs through creator and content lines it scores at 1.
house: Say and do: the Radar ran no house tests on Madwire, so integrity is unread, and it flagged no gaps because the lines it tests (paid search, paid social, LinkedIn, AI search, CRO) are not sold at core here. What the house shows is quiet: the Google Transparency Center holds 0 ads and the LinkedIn Ad Library 0 (the note reads '0 ads match the name query (all advertisers); first results page shows 0 cards'), so a company selling multi channel digital advertising runs none of its own that the record can see. The tag stack is GTM alone, with no social pixels, no test tools, no ABM stack and no CMS reading. It publishes no llms.txt and blocks no AI crawlers; the sitemap lists 81 URLs, 0 updated in 90 days, 0 in 365 days and 0 AI URLs. Social links point to LinkedIn, an Instagram account under the Marketing 360 name, X and Facebook.
market:
Horus puts Madwire at tailwind index -0.7, band Neutral, 17:26 on the Solar Arc. Best placed for KJ8 (human provenance as a distribution signal). Most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle hollowed out, driven by Paid Search and Paid Social) and KJ7 (local discovery being enclosed, driven by Local). Best scenario fit: The Commons Rebuilt at 50/100. It makes no P move outright: partial on P3 (local at depth, no LSA or Sponsored Places work) and P7 (some owned audience work), absent on P1, P2, P6 and P8; P4 does not apply, P5 unknown.

The Monsoon read is 71.7, band Landfall, percentile 92: migration 61.7 against displacement 81.7, so clients leaving on price runs well ahead of hours moving with the company. The sold mix supplies 62 of the index, Web & Product (18) and Local (17) carrying the most movable hours; the work would go 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. Footprint inferred: no hub offices, no onshore claims; SMB client type adds 12 points, scaled segment 8.
openings:
The strongest opening is price: displacement 81.7 on the Monsoon read says the SMB book buys on price, web and local carry the most movable hours, and the record shows no onshore delivery claim to answer with. A rival delivering website build, listings and review management from an offshore bench can very likely (moderate confidence) undercut the platform subscription line by line for the franchise and small business subscribers it claims. Falsifier: a public Madwire price list entering the record below an offshore delivered rival's would weaken it.

The second opening is the missing AI line: no AI search capability, no AI URLs, no llms.txt, and P1 absent, so a rival that sells local AI visibility (what the assistants say about a plumber or a franchise unit) sells something the platform has no page for. The third is local depth without LSAs or Sponsored Places (P3 partial): a rival treating those as core local work offers what the record shows Madwire does not. No public pricing (P5 unknown), no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent). The 15,000 client claim with 0 names is the question to put to its subscribers.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, October 2026: output or outcome pricing at a top five holdco would sharpen the KJ6 exposure of a platform with no public price on record.

I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas or engagement would strengthen the KJ8 tailwind that runs through its creator and content lines.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization, above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and bears on the KJ7 enclosure of local discovery its listings line depends on.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.

The next Radar compile: this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile, the record carries low confidence, and the sitemap had 0 updates in 365 days, so the first sign of life to watch for is any new URL or any own ad.
